Biosphere Scientific Classes

This reference covers all 23 certificate-backed scientific classes in relic.scientific.biosphere: 23 executable concrete Functors, 0 fail-closed unavailable boundaries, and 0 abstract contracts. Each entry is generated from the live class, its IPHS certificate, State Contract Model, and ParameterManager metadata. Fail-closed unavailable classes are not instantiated during documentation generation.

The tables distinguish constructor controls, runtime variables, and ParameterManager scientific parameters. Values shown as package defaults belong to the documented RELIC architecture version and must not be copied as hardcoded constants into scientific code.

Certificate wildcard parameter groups (*, <pft>) are expanded to their exact current YAML entries. Every other declared parameter is matched to the parameter database by its exact full key; a declared name is never mapped to a key that merely ends with the same name.

Exact ParameterManager rows report the live YAML value, bounds, gradient policy, description, and provenance. A row whose value reads not declared in the parameter database is intentionally not assigned an invented default: the class metadata or certificate declares the quantity, with the meaning and units it states, but the parameter database has no key of that exact name.

IPHS levels are read from the sole certificate owner. Levels 1 to 3 describe compatibility, wrapping, or declared structure; they are not strict IPHS/GENERIC claims.

The Channel column of each runtime output contract applies relic.core.state.types.partition_outputs, the only runtime output channel classifier, to the declared output name. A name that the classifier reserves for diagnostics, such as diagnostics.*, goes to the diagnostics channel and is never committed as state. For any other name the channel is decided at run time by the write mode of the returned value: StateWriteMode.DERIVED routes the output to the diagnostics channel, and any other write mode sends it to the StateManager commit (a value without a write mode takes the run’s semantic-mode rules or the StateManager schema). The generator does not run forward(), so it does not predict that write mode. The Kind column is the State Contract Model kind of the variable and does not set its channel.

Composition channels and executable PortSpec API

Certificate composition channels: isoprene_emission, monoterpenes_emission, sesquiterpenes_emission, ovocs_emission, bvoc_carbon_allocation_flux

This class does not expose a class-level executable ports() schema. Certificate channels therefore describe composition evidence, not an instantiated PortSpec API. Metadata dependencies: no direct dependency list is declared; composition uses ports, owners, or graph wiring.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

MEP Pathway:

\[ \mathrm{G3P} + \mathrm{Pyruvate} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{DXS}} \mathrm{DXP} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{DXR}} \mathrm{MEP} \longrightarrow \mathrm{DMAPP} \]

Isoprene Synthesis:

\[ \mathrm{DMAPP} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{IS}} \mathrm{Isoprene} \]
\[ J_{\mathrm{DXS}} = V_{\mathrm{max},\mathrm{DXS}} \cdot [ \mathrm{G3P} ] \cdot [ \mathrm{Pyr} ] / ( ( K_{\mathrm{G3P}} + [ \mathrm{G3P} ] ) \cdot ( K_{\mathrm{Pyr}} + [ \mathrm{Pyr} ] ) ) \]
\[ J_{\mathrm{IS}} ( T_{\mathrm{air}} ) = V_{\mathrm{max},\mathrm{IS}} ( T_{\mathrm{air}} ) \cdot [ \mathrm{DMAPP} ] / ( K_{\mathrm{DMAPP}} + [ \mathrm{DMAPP} ] ) \cdot K_{\mathrm{CO2}} / ( K_{\mathrm{CO2}} + C_{a} ) \]
\[ A_{\mathrm{ATP}} = J_{\mathrm{DMAPP}} \cdot \nu_{\mathrm{ATP}}; A_{\mathrm{NADPH}} = J_{\mathrm{DMAPP}} \cdot \nu_{\mathrm{NADPH}} \]

The exact proxy and kinetic closure is ParameterManager-backed and is not claimed as a universal leaf-scale law.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

\(L_{\mathrm{eff}} = ( 1 - \exp ( - k \mathrm{LAI} ) ) / k \mathrm{maps} \mathrm{leaf} - \mathrm{area} \mathrm{kinetics}\) to ground-area ports

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Stored-pool studies support separating synthesis from release and a strong temperature response of release. The exact GPP saturation, Q10 synthesis, capacity limiter, and degradation coefficients are calibratable ParameterManager-backed phenomenological choices, not a universal source law.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

air temperature, gross photosynthesis, and pool concentration are empirical drivers; no thermodynamic effort is claimed

state_advancer

the bounded pool ledger is evaluated once, and its rate and port cochains are evaluated as \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) by advance_reaction_network with an explicit identity \(N_{h}\)

runtime_usage

MonoterpeneSynthesis.forward evaluates one bounded storage ledger, exposes its residual, and wraps the resulting rate and port cochains through the existing reaction-network runtime.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

the identity \(N_{h}\) wrapper covers emission, synthesis, positive plant-carbon allocation, degradation, pool-tendency, storage-carbon, and boundary-residual cochains; this is level-2 wrapping rather than strict stoichiometric closure.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

The light factor is Guenther et al. (2012) Eq. (3) with the Table 4 sesquiterpene light-dependent fraction and the Eq. (4) light-dependent activity; the temperature factor is the Eq. (7) blend of the Eq. (11) exponential about the MEGAN standard temperature T_s and the Eq. (8) light-dependent response, with the Table 4 Other Sesquiterpenes row; stress is the most limiting supplied factor. The RELIC reduced closure converts a dry-leaf-mass-normalized factor through LAI k_f; it is not the canonical MEGAN2.1 vegetation-type, ground-area emission-factor formulation. Stored-emitter literature requires synthesis and release to remain distinct when storage is represented; this no-storage closure reports emitted compound carbon only as an explicit allocation proxy.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

ParameterManager-backed thermodynamic effort, driver, or diagnostic input used by the module

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

SesquiterpeneSynthesis.forward validates the declared state ports, evaluates one MEGAN-family empirical response rate, maps the mass-normalized rate through required LAI and ParameterManager-backed \(k_{f}\), converts it through the existing UnitConverter, derives the positive no-storage plant-carbon allocation proxy, calls advance_reaction_network with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates, and emits the canonical molar and carbon ports plus namespaced diagnostics.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

SesquiterpeneSynthesis.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network with open_system_route=port.

fixed

Standard temperature T_s of the light-independent Eq. (11) response exp(beta (T - T_s)); 303.15 K (30 degC) is paired with the reference temperature of the RELIC dry-mass emission factors (basal emission rates normalized to 30 degC; standard air temperature 303 K of the MEGAN canopy factors). kg C m-2 s-1

diagnostics

NPP minus the three allocated organ fluxes

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(\frac{\mathrm{d}B_{i}}{\mathrm{d}t} = f_{i} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} )\), with \(\sum_{i} ( f_{i} ) = 1\), construction respiration accounted before NPP, and the BVOC debit enabled only by an explicit graph-selected owner

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(r_{h} = f_{i} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} )\), ParameterManager-backed allocation coefficients, and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_{h}\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit three-channel identity wrapper for leaf, wood, and root allocation rates

r_h

vector \([ f_{\mathrm{leaf}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) , f_{\mathrm{stem}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) , f_{\mathrm{root}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) ]\) evaluated once by the production forward path

boundary_route

net_primary_productivity and the graph-selected bvoc_carbon_allocation_flux close the local partition; growth_rate_leaf, growth_rate_stem, and growth_rate_root are the only carbon.total input boundaries for the tracked structural stocks

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

empirical NPP boundary flux and allocation controls; no Hamiltonian effort is claimed at level 2

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with a three-channel identity \(N_{h}\) and \(r_{h} = [ f_{\mathrm{leaf}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) , f_{\mathrm{stem}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) , f_{\mathrm{root}} \cdot ( \mathrm{NPP} - F_{\mathrm{BVOC},C} ) ]\)

runtime_usage

BiomassAllocation.forward resolves the graph-selected BVOC debit, normalizes organ fractions, evaluates all three rates once through advance_reaction_network, and emits the integrated state_delta as per-step ACCUMULATE updates.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

The identity \(N_{h}\) wrapper is explicit level-2 runtime structure and is not strict stoichiometric, Hamiltonian, or GENERIC evidence.

Composition channels and executable PortSpec API

Certificate composition channels: net_primary_productivity, bvoc_carbon_allocation_flux, leaf_biomass_c, wood_biomass_c, root_biomass_c

This class does not expose a class-level executable ports() schema. Certificate channels therefore describe composition evidence, not an instantiated PortSpec API. Metadata dependencies: no direct dependency list is declared; composition uses ports, owners, or graph wiring.

validation.numerical.response.ph_optimum

Default optimal pH for generic biological responses. The pH of dilute aqueous soil solutions lies on the 0-14 scale. This runtime metadata binding is optional.

Source: response_defaults; General soil chemistry practice

dimensionless

Default width for pH response curve. A response width in pH units cannot be negative; no physical upper limit is fixed, so the upper bound is open (inf). This runtime metadata binding is optional.

Source: response_defaults; General soil chemistry practice

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ r_{\mathrm{growth}} = \mathrm{SLA} \cdot \mathrm{growth}_{\mathrm{rate},\mathrm{leaf}}; r_{\mathrm{loss}} = k_{\mathrm{leaf}} \cdot \mathrm{leaf}_{\mathrm{area},\mathrm{index}}; r_{\mathrm{net}} = r_{\mathrm{growth}} - r_{\mathrm{loss}} \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{y} = N_{h} r_{h}; \delta_{y} = \dot{y} \cdot \mathrm{d}t \]

Entry

Meaning

N_h

signed row \([ 1 , - 1 ]\) mapping gross leaf-area growth and senescence to the net observation

r_h

explicit \([ \mathrm{SLA} \cdot \mathrm{growth}_{\mathrm{rate},\mathrm{leaf}} , k_{\mathrm{leaf}} \cdot \mathrm{leaf}_{\mathrm{area},\mathrm{index}} ]\) tendency channels

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

one diagnostic leaf-area observation row

effort_variable

required growth_rate_leaf and leaf_area_index inputs with ParameterManager-backed SLA and turnover coefficients

state_advancer

observation \(\dot{y} = N_{h} r_{h}\); \(\delta_{y} = \dot{y} \cdot \mathrm{d}t\)

runtime_usage

StructuralGrowth.forward reads the net tendency and step delta returned by advance_reaction_network without advancing leaf_area_index.

species=(diagnostics.structural_growth.net_leaf_area_tendency); reactions=(leaf_area_growth, leaf_area_senescence); \(\mathrm{stoichiometric}_{N} = [ [ 1 , - 1 ] ] .\)

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Crop phenology equations:

Daily thermal time:

\[ PHU_{daily} = \max(0, T_{avg} - T_{base}) \]

Cumulative PHU:

\[ PHU_{cum} = \sum_{i=sowing}^{t} PHU_{daily,i} \]

Development index:

\[ DI = \frac{PHU_{cum}}{PHU_{total}} \]

Harvest index dynamics:

\[ HI(t) = HI_{max} \times \frac{DI - DI_{HI-start}}{1 - DI_{HI-start}} \]
\[ \text{ for } DI \geq DI_{HI-start} \]

Biomass partitioning:

\[ f_{grain} = HI(t) \text{ during grain filling} \]
\[ f_{leaf} = (1 - HI(t)) \times allocation_{leaf}(DI) \]
\[ f_{stem} = (1 - HI(t)) \times allocation_{stem}(DI) \]
\[ f_{root} = (1 - HI(t)) \times allocation_{root}(DI) \]

Development stages:

  • Germination: \(0 < \mathrm{DI} < 0.15\)

  • Vegetative: \(0.15 < \mathrm{DI} < 0.4\)

  • Reproductive: \(0.4 < \mathrm{DI} < 0.65\)

  • Grain filling: \(0.65 < \mathrm{DI} < 1.0\)

  • \(Maturity: DI \geq 1.0\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

ParameterManager-backed thermodynamic effort, driver, or diagnostic input used by the module

state_advancer

C and N turnover uses \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network; crop temporal full states use the canonical StateManager replacement path.

runtime_usage

CropPhenology inherits PhenologyBase.forward, which calls advance_reaction_network for the C and N turnover ledger and emits explicit REPLACE updates for the complete crop temporal state.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

PhenologyBase.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates for the C and N turnover outputs and lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network; PHU and crop-cycle memory are not misrepresented as reaction states.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

GDD phenology equations:

Daily GDD:

\[ GDD_{daily} = \max(0, \frac{T_{max} + T_{min}}{2} - T_{base}) \]

Cumulative GDD:

\[ GDD_{cum} = \sum_{i=1}^{t} GDD_{daily,i} \]

Growth factor:

\[\begin{split} f_{growth}(GDD_{cum}) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } GDD_{cum} < GDD_{start} \\ \frac{GDD_{cum} - GDD_{start}}{GDD_{full} - GDD_{start}} & \text{if } GDD_{start} \leq GDD_{cum} < GDD_{full} \\ 1 & \text{if } GDD_{full} \leq GDD_{cum} < GDD_{end} \\ 1 - \frac{GDD_{cum} - GDD_{end}}{GDD_{senes} - GDD_{end}} & \text{if } GDD_{end} \leq GDD_{cum} < GDD_{senes} \\ 0 & \text{if } GDD_{cum} \geq GDD_{senes} \end{cases} \end{split}\]
\[ LAI(t) = LAI_{max} \times f_{growth}(GDD_{cum}(t)) \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

ParameterManager-backed thermodynamic effort, driver, or diagnostic input used by the module

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

GDDPhenology inherits PhenologyBase.forward, which calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting canonical phenology outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

PhenologyBase.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates for GDDPhenology outputs, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

Composition channels and executable PortSpec API

This class does not expose a class-level executable ports() schema. Certificate channels therefore describe composition evidence, not an instantiated PortSpec API. Metadata dependencies: no direct dependency list is declared; composition uses ports, owners, or graph wiring.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ \mathrm{iGSI} = f_{T} ( T_{\mathrm{min}} ) f_{\mathrm{VPD}} ( \mathrm{VPD} ) f_{\mathrm{day}} ( \mathrm{daylength} ); \mathrm{GSI}_{\mathrm{bar},n} = \operatorname{mean} ( \mathrm{iGSI} \mathrm{over} \mathrm{the} 21 - \mathrm{day} \mathrm{StateManager} \mathrm{window} ) . \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

ParameterManager-backed thermodynamic effort, driver, or diagnostic input used by the module

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

GSIPhenology inherits PhenologyBase.forward, which calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting canonical phenology outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

PhenologyBase.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates for GSIPhenology outputs, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Static phenology equations:

Growth factor:

\[\begin{split} f_{growth}(t) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } t < t_{onset} \\ 0.5(1 + \tanh(k(t - t_{onset}))) & \text{if } t_{onset} \leq t < t_{full} \\ 1 & \text{if } t_{full} \leq t < t_{senes} \\ 0.5(1 + \tanh(k(t_{offset} - t))) & \text{if } t_{senes} \leq t < t_{offset} \\ 0 & \text{if } t \geq t_{offset} \end{cases} \end{split}\]
\[ LAI(t) = LAI_{max} \times f_{growth}(t) \]

Where:

  • t: day of year [days]

  • t_{onset}: leaf onset date [DOY]

  • t_{offset}: leaf offset date [DOY]

  • \(t_{full} = t_{onset} + expansion_{days}\)

  • \(t_{senes} = t_{offset} - senescence_{days}\)

  • \(k = \mathrm{transition}_{\mathrm{steepness}}\): transition steepness [day-1]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ A = \min ( \mathrm{Ac} , \mathrm{Aj} ) - \mathrm{Rd}; \mathrm{Ac} = V_{c,\max} \cdot ( \mathrm{Ci} - \Gamma_{\star} ) / ( \mathrm{Ci} + K_c \cdot ( 1 + O / K_o ) ); \mathrm{Aj} = J \cdot ( \mathrm{Ci} - \Gamma_{\star} ) / ( 4 \cdot ( \mathrm{Ci} + 2 \cdot \Gamma_{\star} ) ) \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

open gross-assimilation, net-assimilation, and dark-respiration output ports

effort_variable

atmospheric CO2, PPFD, VPD, temperature, and optional control drivers; no thermodynamic effort proof is claimed

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) uses an identity-like output incidence and advance_reaction_network with open_system_route=port

runtime_usage

FarquharPhotosynthesis.forward calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting canonical outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

FarquharPhotosynthesis.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ R_{\mathrm{auto}} = R_{\mathrm{maintenance}} + R_{\mathrm{growth}}; \mathrm{NPP} = \mathrm{GPP} - R_{\mathrm{auto}} \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with scheduler-provided carbon-port rates \(r_{h}\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_{h}\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

scheduler state-port vector [GPP, \(R_{m}\), \(R_{g}\)] evaluated by the production forward path; the diagnostic epsilon is not a rate

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

no thermodynamic effort is claimed at level 2; gross_primary_productivity is the declared carbon input port

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(r_{h} = [ \mathrm{GPP} , R_{m} , R_{g} ]\) and rows for \(R_{a}\) and NPP

runtime_usage

AutotrophicRespiration.forward reads all three scheduler state inputs, then evaluates total respiration and NPP through advance_reaction_network.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

\(N_{h}\) rows are \([ 0 , 1 , 1 ]\) for \(R_{a}\) and \([ 1 , - 1 , - 1 ]\) for NPP.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(F_{\mathrm{O3}} = ( g_{s} / k_{\mathrm{O3}} ) \cdot [ \mathrm{O}_{3} ] \cdot \mathrm{ozone}_{\mathrm{uptake},\mathrm{rate}}\), \(\mathrm{the} R_{a} \rightarrow 0 \mathrm{limit} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{Sitch} \mathrm{et} \mathrm{al} . ( 2007 ) \mathrm{leaf} \mathrm{uptake} [ \mathrm{O}_{3} ] / ( R_{a} + k_{\mathrm{O3}} / g_{l} )\) with \(g_{s}\) the leaf-level stomatal conductance to water vapour and \(k_{\mathrm{O3}} = 1.67\); \(f_{\mathrm{O3}} = 1 - \min ( F_{\mathrm{O3}} / C_{\mathrm{detox}} , r_{\mathrm{max}} )\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(r_{h} = [ F_{\mathrm{O3}} , \min ( F_{\mathrm{O3}} , C_{\mathrm{detox}} ) , \max ( F_{\mathrm{O3}} - C_{\mathrm{detox}} , 0 ) ]\) and open port routing.

Entry

Meaning

declared stoichiometric/output incidence matrix in OzoneStress.forward.

r_h

ParameterManager-backed reaction-rate vector [\(F_{\mathrm{O3}}\), detoxification_flux, excess_ozone_flux].

G_h

open atmospheric ozone uptake port declared through open_system_route='port'.

y_h

ozone exposure effort \([ \mathrm{O}_{3} ] / [ \mathrm{O}_{3} ] _ \mathrm{threshold}\) used for port-power audit.

relic.physical.constants.conversions.h2o_o3_diffusivity_ratio

dimensionless

1.67; bounds=(1.67, 1.67)

fixed

Diffusivity ratio of water vapor to ozone in air: the ratio k_O3 of the leaf (stomatal) resistance for O3 to that for water vapor, so that the stomatal conductance for O3 is g_s,O3 = g_s,H2O / k_O3

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Rectangular-hyperbola PPFD response and fixed-Q10 empirical respiration response, with positive-to-atmosphere \(\mathrm{NEE} = \mathrm{Reco} - \mathrm{GPP}\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(y_{h} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(r_{h} = [ \mathrm{GPP} , \mathrm{Reco} ]\) and \(N_{h}\) rows [1,0], [0,1], [-1,1]

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC open carbon-flux port basis

effort_variable

not claimed for this level 2 empirical reaction wrapper

state_advancer

\(y_{h} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

SimpleCanopyPhotosynthesis.forward calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting canonical outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

SimpleCanopyPhotosynthesis.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

biosphere.photosynthesis.surrogate.max_gpp_rate

kg C m-2 s-1

3e-07; bounds=(1e-08, 1e-06)

fixed

Maximum gross primary productivity of the surrogate canopy model per unit leaf area index at saturating light and optimum temperature and soil moisture (3.0e-7 kg C m-2 s-1 is about 25 umol CO2 m-2 s-1); the ground-area rate is this value times the light, temperature and soil moisture factors and the leaf area index; the upper bound equals validation.conservation.plausibility.gross_primary_productivity_max

Source: model_default; Monteith & Unsworth (2013) Principles of Environmental Physics; Baldocchi (2003) Global Change Biology 9:479-492

umol photons m-2 s-1

600.0; bounds=(100.0, 1500.0)

fixed

Half-saturation PPFD for the surrogate rectangular-hyperbola light response

Source: model_default; Baly & Morgan (1934) Nature 133:414

biosphere.photosynthesis.surrogate.base_respiration_rate

kg C m-2 s-1

4.8e-08; bounds=(1e-09, 1e-06)

fixed

Ecosystem respiration rate of the surrogate module per unit leaf area index at the physical-constant reference temperature (4.8e-8 kg C m-2 s-1 is about 4 umol CO2 m-2 s-1); the ground-area rate is this value times the Q10 temperature factor and the leaf area index; the upper bound equals validation.conservation.plausibility.gross_primary_productivity_max

Source: model_default; Mahecha et al. (2010) Science 329:838-840; Baldocchi (2003) Global Change Biology 9:479-492

dimensionless

Source: literature; Mahecha et al. (2010) Science 329:838-840
